jurisdiction.venue: U.S. District Court for the Eastern District of New York, Central Islip

headline: Long Island Father and Son Plead Guilty in $600 Million COVID Tax-Credit Mill Run Out of ‘Credit Reset’
deck: Keith Williams and Jamari Lewis admitted filing more than 8,000 bogus employment tax returns claiming over $600 million in pandemic payroll credits—extracting $46.76 million from the IRS before their guilty pleas in Central Islip.

street_crime_compare.exec_summary: West Hempstead father and son Keith Williams and Jamari Lewis pleaded guilty in E.D.N.Y. to filing over 8,000 fraudulent COVID-19 tax returns seeking $600 million+ (receiving $46.76 million), agreeing to $46.76 million in IRS restitution ahead of sentencing.
street_crime_compare.street_equivalent: Mailing 8,000 fabricated municipal rebate coupons from a storefront office until the city treasury mails back $46.7 million in real checks
street_crime_compare.street_sentence: Mandatory multi-year federal felony imprisonment under Sentencing Guidelines, with statutory wire-fraud caps of 30 years

sources.title: New York Father and Son Plead Guilty in $600M Covid Tax Fraud Scheme
sources.agency: U.S. Department of Justice, Office of Public Affairs

interactive_art_spec.caption: The Alfonse M. D’Amato United States Courthouse in Central Islip, New York, where Keith Williams and Jamari Lewis pleaded guilty in a $600 million COVID-19 employment tax-credit conspiracy.
